title: What Do Llamas Really Think? Revealing Preference Biases in Language Model Representations
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures implicit preference biases of LLMs in the domain of religion. Specifically, it tests for preference between the three major Abrahamic religions (Christianity, Islam, Judaism) and between reformationist vs. conservative branches within those religions.
findings: The study found significant religious biases in the LLMs tested. Models were evenly split in their preference for Christianity (62% average win rate) and Judaism (58%), while none of the models preferred Islam (45%). This aligns with previous findings associating Islam with violence in language models. The paper attributes this to the negative representation of Islam in the English-language internet corpora used for training. Additionally, almost all LLMs showed a preference for less orthodox (reformationist) branches over conservative ones.
